newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Congress expels 13 deputies for graft.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Congress expels 13 deputies for graft.

text.p: Ecuador's Congress in an unprecedented move expelled 13 deputies accused of corruption on Thursday while four others remained under suspicion, authorities said.
The legislators, including the brother of former President Abdala Bucaram, were charged with the unauthorised use of state funds. Their case will be taken up by the Supreme Court.
The Constitution bans legislators from handling state funds. They were expelled after a special parliamentary committee investigated 34 of Congress' 84 deputies for graft.

In a special marathon session that ended in the early hours of Thursday, 54 deputies voted to throw out their colleagues. It was the first time in Ecuadorean history that Congress has expelled members for corruption.

Those ousted included 10 independent deputies, two from the Roldosista party, including Santiago Bucaram, and two from the Conservative party. Three other independent and one Roldosista deputies remain under investigation.

Bucaram, whose brother was ousted from the presidency in February on grounds of mental incompentence, was accused of a million-dollar fraud against the state through the sale of obsolete computers to state-run schools.
